kf: **Alopecia areata** is autoimmune, **non-scarring** hair loss in round or oval patches with normal-looking skin.
**Exclamation-mark hairs** at the edge; can affect beard, brows, lashes and nails (pitting).
Severe forms: **ophiasis** (band along the hairline), totalis (whole scalp) and universalis (all body hair).
About 80% of small, short-duration patches regrow within a year, but relapse is common.
Adults: potent or very potent scalp steroid for about 3 months (off-label); refer children, extensive or distressing disease (JAK inhibitors are specialist).

sub: Lifetime risk about 2%; any age, often starting in childhood or young adulthood.
Associated with atopy, thyroid disease, vitiligo and Down syndrome.

aet: Loss of the hair follicle's **immune privilege** with CD8+ T-cell attack; genetic susceptibility (HLA, ULBP3).
myths: **"Stress alone causes it"**: it is autoimmune; stress may trigger flares.
**"Hair loss is permanent"**: follicles are not destroyed, so regrowth is possible even after years.
patho_lead: Immune cells attack **growing (anagen) hair bulbs** but spare the stem cells, so hair can regrow.

mech.t: Anagen bulbs normally hide their antigens (low MHC class I); in AA this privilege fails.
Interferon-γ and **JAK–STAT** signalling recruit CD8+ T cells around the bulb ('swarm of bees'): the target of JAK inhibitors.
Damaged hairs narrow near the scalp and break: **exclamation-mark hairs**; follicles enter early catagen and telogen.
Stem cells in the bulge survive, so regrowth often starts as fine white hairs that later repigment.

histo: Peribulbar lymphocytic infiltrate around anagen follicles; increased catagen/telogen hairs; no scarring. Biopsy only if the diagnosis is uncertain.

sub: Refer; use lower-potency steroids, and consider the psychosocial impact and school support.
Fine regular pitting or trachyonychia in 10–20%, more with severe disease.

comp: Loss of eyelashes and brows (eye irritation).
prog: Unpredictable. Worse outlook: onset in childhood, extensive or ophiasis pattern, nail disease, atopy, long duration.
